incidents.victim: Fireworks AI (cascading to Uber, Cursor, Notion)
incidents.vector: Stolen credentials issued to AI training platform Fireworks were used to breach its infrastructure, then reused to pivot into customer environments including Cursor's extension marketplace and an Uber cloud storage environment.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole billing and AI-specific data from Fireworks, uploaded a malicious Claude Code VS Code extension to Cursor's marketplace that installed SSH backdoors on roughly 5,000 systems, and accessed driver's license images and PII for 149,346 people via a third-party cloud environment tied to Uber.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor manufacturers, US defense-policy organizations, and civil-society groups (19 targeted, 10 breached)
incidents.vector: Attackers supplied a target and goal to the open-source autonomous AI pentesting framework Cairn, paired with Chinese LLMs (Zhipu GLM, DeepSeek), which then independently planned, scanned, and exploited known weaknesses — weak/default credentials, auth bypasses, exposed APIs — with minimal human direction.
incidents.impact: Across 25 autonomous operations run in August-September 2026, the campaign achieved unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 organizations, exposing over 1 million personal records at one victim, obtaining military and government identities, and creating persistent administrator accounts in a production system.

incidents.victim: French media, entertainment, and education-sector websites
incidents.vector: A system dubbed "exploit_agent" chains multiple AI agents and language models to automatically compare vendor code before and after a patch ships, infer the underlying flaw, draft a working exploit, and execute it — entirely without a human in the loop.
incidents.impact: Google's Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant assess this as the first cyberattack run end-to-end by AI; victim data on the attacker's staging server pointed to targeting of French websites, though Google stopped short of confirming the scale of any successful compromise.

incidents.victim: 2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants managed by MSPs (via ConnectWise Cloud Backup/SkyKick)
incidents.industry: Managed service providers / multi-tenant IT services
incidents.vector: A stolen ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) application credential — a highly privileged app consented across many customer tenants — gave the attacker access to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants managed by MSPs.
incidents.impact: Microsoft, Huntress, and CyberDrain jointly helped contain the intrusion and shipped detections; the full scope of data accessed across affected tenants has not been disclosed.

incidents.victim: Organizations across multiple industry sectors worldwide
incidents.vector: Phishing emails impersonating Microsoft 365 service-health notifications claimed held messages would be deleted within 24 hours, directing recipients to a fake "RESTORE MESSAGES" link leading to an off-brand credential-phishing page. The campaign also exploited public attention on a prior Microsoft 365 outage as a lure.
incidents.impact: Microsoft assesses the activity as likely intended to capture credentials; no confirmed credential theft or post-compromise activity has been observed, and known malicious domains are blocked by Microsoft Defender.

incidents.victim: Lithuania Customs (state agency)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a poorly secured technical function to gain unauthorized access to the agency's main user-management portal (BAP), used by individuals, businesses, and EU customs systems.
incidents.impact: Personal data (names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, national ID numbers) of several hundred individuals and businesses may have been exposed; investigators believe attackers attempted to penetrate deeper into systems holding more sensitive data. EU customs platforms, including Import Control System 2, were disrupted.

incidents.victim: Unidentified Romanian government institution
incidents.vector: A Russian FSB-linked espionage group exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft software to infiltrate a government email server, using a toolkit configured to collect emails exchanged with NATO and EU institutions.
incidents.impact: Romania's intelligence service (SRI) detected and contained the December 2025 intrusion and restored the affected email service; no evidence was found that sensitive information was stolen. Russia has denied involvement.

incidents.victim: U.S. hospitals, healthcare entities, and schools in at least six states
incidents.vector: Members of the INC/Lynx-affiliated "8-Digits Team" gained network access to victim organizations, exfiltrated data, then extorted victims by threatening to publicly release the stolen records.
incidents.impact: The group claimed possession of over 50 terabytes of data, including more than 70 million confidential health records, generating over $500 million in ransom demands. A key member, Roman Khlynovskiy, was extradited from Italy to face trial in the U.S.

incidents.victim: Barracuda Networks (internal cloud environment)
incidents.vector: An un-revoked cloud access key issued to a third-party AI service provider let an attacker into Barracuda's cloud, where they deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across 10 internal cloud environments.
incidents.impact: The attacker searched for cryptocurrency wallet data (seed phrases, private keys) across environments, including some supporting Barracuda's XDR platform; no evidence was found that XDR customer credentials were accessed, but affected customers were told to reissue credentials as a precaution.

incidents.victim: Quantum Systems (German defense/drone manufacturer supplying Ukraine)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached Quantum Systems' drone flight-planning software and planted a malicious update.
incidents.impact: Quantum Systems shut down its IT network and German defense forces grounded drones as a precaution while investigating; the company says the malicious file was never delivered to any drones.

incidents.victim: City of Mobile, Alabama (municipal government)
incidents.vector: Scammers posed as a legitimate contractor over roughly five months, convincing city staff to change the contractor's payment and bank account details.
incidents.impact: The city paid $14.7 million to the fraudsters; the scheme was discovered about a week after the final payment, when the real contractor reported a missing payment.

incidents.victim: City of Osaka (municipal government)
incidents.vector: Hackers compromised the city's third-party email service provider.
incidents.impact: Personal data of roughly 1 million Osaka citizens was stolen.

incidents.victim: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a cloud service provider used by TSMC (the company says its own network was not breached) and attempted to extort $200,000 in Bitcoin.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 46,000 TSMC employees was leaked on an underground hacking forum after TSMC did not pay the ransom.

incidents.victim: Caribbean Airlines (via Amadeus reservation platform)
incidents.vector: Compromise of Spanish airline-reservation platform Amadeus exposed passenger data across multiple airline customers, including Caribbean Airlines.
incidents.impact: Passenger data was exposed as part of a broader Amadeus platform breach affecting numerous airlines.

incidents.victim: Maileva (subsidiary of La Poste Group, France)
incidents.vector: Unspecified compromise of Maileva's online mail and parcel-delivery platform.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 22 million users was stolen, most of them corporate employees who received paychecks, invoices, and business mail through the platform.

incidents.victim: Trezor and Ledger hardware wallet customers
incidents.vector: A compromised reseller (CryptoBillis) distributed hardware wallets implanted with covert spy chips to customers who bought devices between August and September 2026.
incidents.impact: Trezor shipped a firmware update to brick the backdoored devices and cut 80% of its supplier network; the same supplier was separately linked to spy devices found in Ledger wallets.

incidents.victim: ActiveCloud (Belarusian cloud hosting provider)
incidents.vector: Unspecified ransomware intrusion; no group has publicly taken credit.
incidents.impact: Web hosting and email services were restored, but other services remained down nearly a week after the attack; three other Russian cloud providers were hit by similar unexplained incidents in the preceding month.

incidents.victim: CSCTelecom (Latvian branch, telecommunications provider)
incidents.vector: An unsecured, publicly accessible database containing over 125 million SMS messages was left exposed online.
incidents.impact: More than 125 million SMS messages, potentially including sensitive message content, were exposed to anyone who found the database.

incidents.victim: Expedia Group
incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Expedia's network via a third-party data platform provider.
incidents.impact: The n0n data-extortion group leaked Expedia data online after the company refused to pay a ransom; Expedia is the world's second-largest travel agency by revenue.

incidents.victim: Arcus (cryptocurrency exchange)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a flaw in Arcus's user-accounting system to withdraw funds they were not entitled to.
incidents.impact: $2.23 million in crypto assets was stolen; the platform's withdrawal rate limit blocked an additional $3 million from leaving before it could be drained.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric-vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers took over master user accounts for Li Auto vehicles, likely via compromised Chinese eSIMs used to register the accounts, locking legitimate owners out of their cars.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed vehicle owners were locked out of their cars and extorted to regain control; the actual number of affected vehicles is believed to be higher.

incidents.victim: Government entities in Southeast Asia, South America, and Europe
incidents.vector: Server exploitation (unpatched Exchange and web servers, web shells) and phishing with decoy PDFs delivered two custom RATs — PerfectPioneer and its successor KUKURAT — which use HTTP/3 (QUIC) for stealthy command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Active since at least mid-2025, the group has conducted long-term, high-stealth intelligence collection and data exfiltration against government targets, continuously upgrading its tradecraft through early 2026.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations in the US and Europe with internet-exposed VPN appliances
incidents.vector: TAG-218 compromised SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks, and Fortinet VPN appliances — including via a GlobalProtect authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-0257) — then pivoted to the virtualization layer, deploying a previously undocumented ESXi implant ("GhostFrame") to harvest credentials and control guest virtual machines.
incidents.impact: Four victim organizations tied to this infrastructure were subsequently published on the Settra ransomware leak site; GhostFrame gives attackers centralized access to credentials and VMs across an entire compromised hypervisor.

incidents.victim: Supermarkets, food retailers, and medical facilities across France and 10+ European countries
incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to internet-exposed refrigeration controllers — likely via vulnerable firmware or default credentials — and set units to defrost mode, raising temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F), in some cases causing fires.
incidents.impact: Roughly 700 French supermarkets were hit in an Oct 11-12 wave, followed by a second wave on Nov 1-2 affecting 100-115 more retail locations across 10+ countries; medical-facility refrigeration was also affected (no evidence blood products spoiled). French authorities formally attributed the campaign to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit, citing tens of millions of euros in losses.
